# Marvin Simulator for Windows: port plan **Status:** final, revised after the review, 2026-10-04. **Baseline:** - Repository /Users/m1/marvin, branch `codex/mos-aster-racing-city`, HEAD `1c8bb11`, game target `apps/simulator-macos`. - The repository (github.com/entireio/marvin) is **public**. That affects licensing (§9) and CI security (§6.2). **Inputs:** - The 8-reader inventory and the completeness critic: 161 platform dependencies (87 low, 54 medium, 17 high and 3 very high difficulty) and 246 fidelity-spec rows. - The three proposals, the two judgements and the review of the previous draft. - A read-only inspection of the repo and of the local macOS SDK headers. - Web verification of third-party technology. **Markers:** - Sources are tagged [S#] and listed in Appendix B. - **(unverified)** marks a claim I could not confirm. Appendix C collects these. - Appendix A corrects claims made in the proposals. Appendix D lists what changed in response to the review. **Velocity, checked in git:** - 80 simulator commits since 2026-09-26, at 6, 7, 2, 4, 15, 15, 17 and 14 per day. All have one human author, who directs agents. - 61 of the 80 touched render, scene or HUD files. 42 changed shader-modifier or material text. 36 touched SimulationCore. - Hot files: App.swift was touched by 49 commits, TownWorld.swift by 27, DirtWorld.swift by 25 and TownSmoke.swift by 25. --- ## 1. Goal and scope ### 1.1 Goal Ship a native Windows build of Marvin Simulator with the same features and the same graphics as the macOS SceneKit build at the same commit. The Mac game must keep shipping and developing at 10-17 agent commits a day. **Supported Windows versions:** - Windows 11 x64, version 25H2 or later. The reference and benchmark machines run 25H2. - 24H2 is a compatibility test only. Home and Pro servicing ends on 2026-10-13; Enterprise and Education servicing ends on 2027-10-12 [S42]. - 23H2 is unsupported. Home and Pro servicing ended on 2025-11-11 [S42]. - Windows 10 is not tested. ARM64 is optional (§11). There is no compatibility-layer shortcut. SceneKit, AppKit, AVFoundation and Apple's `simd` module have no Windows implementation, so the port has to be done at source level. ### 1.2 What "same features" means operationally **Feature checklist.** `parity/feature-checklist.json` is generated from `inventory.json`. It holds all 246 fidelity-spec rows: 241 from the readers and 5 from the critic. Each row ends either implemented and verified (by a named test or capture) or waived by you. Gate G3 requires 100%. **User-visible scope:** - **Main menu:** live 3D portrait of the 4 robots, the hidden B/R/W/M letters and the 6 persisted settings. - **Sandbox.** - **Race:** the 3-lap Dirt Track with 4 racers, AI, assists and robot collisions. - **Weather and light:** a 10% sandstorm chance per race and per reset, and twin-sun daylight. - **Mos Aster town:** - 497 buildings, 282 people, 27 signs and 13 streets; - 92 + 173 cells with LOD and exploration fades; - residents, street walkers and sliding doors. - **Track surroundings:** the gate (G key), the apron and the city exit. - **Terrain effects:** dunes with deformable sand, trails, debris and robot coating. - **Post-race:** escape into town and roaming. - **Navigation and cameras:** COURSE/TOWN/DUNES maps, camera modes and intro/outro flights. - **Screens:** HUDs, FPS readout, loading screen, scores, pause and focus semantics, and mute. - **Audio:** 30 loop voices, 20 one-shot slots and the voice lines. - **Input:** keyboard and mouse. **Behaviour parity is tolerance-based, not bit-identical.** - libm and FMA differ between platforms, and the 4-robot race is chaotic: its totals already span 90.3-101.5 s across frame rates. - The 39 SimulationChecks must pass on Windows. - A tolerance may change only with your recorded approval and a root-cause note (G0). The known candidate is the coupled-race spread limit: 12 s, against a recorded 11.16 s. - Long runs are compared statistically. **Developer contract.** These stay the same, so `check-sustained-performance.py`, the docs and `docs/simulator-agent-rules.md` §10 keep working: - the smoke and benchmark flags (63, minus the Apple-only diagnostics in §1.4); - the ~23 `MARVIN_*` variables; - output-directory semantics, exit codes and JSON schemas. ### 1.3 What "same graphics" means operationally 1. **Identical inputs by construction.** - Geometry, procedural textures, material parameters, camera maths and simulation state all come from the same Swift generators, seeds and assets. - The town layout hash must be equal on macOS, Linux and Windows. That covers both vector maths and transcendental functions (§4.1). Otherwise you approve an alternative (§11). 2. **Identical render configuration.** - **Race:** - 1920x1080 with 2x MSAA; two shadowed suns with world-anchored, texel-snapped 4096/2048 maps 116 m wide. - SSAO 0.70/1.6/0.025, HDR with fixed exposure, and bloom 0.38/1.2/12. - Linear fog: 115-240 m clear, 3-65 m in a storm. - A procedural sky plus a 64x32 IBL probe. - LOD switches at 8/10/24/26/82/130/260 m. - Reverse-Z with the near plane at 0.02 m. - **Sandbox and menu:** LDR with 4x MSAA, one deferred-shadow light each, and SceneKit's automatic shadow-projection fit (characterised in §5.2). The sandbox has fog at 15-38 m. 3. **Measured shading parity** against SceneKit renders of a frozen scenario table at the same commit: - metrics are object-ID coverage, FLIP, ΔE00 and SSIM per region; - thresholds come from measured noise floors (§5.5). 4. **Human acceptance per area**, as the rules require. You and the Astra judge review contact sheets and motion side-by-sides. A passing metric is never acceptance. **Deviations agreed in advance (each needs your yes in §11):** - **Fonts.** SF Pro, SF Mono and Avenir Next cannot ship [S28][S30], so the HUD layout is re-baselined after the font switch (§5.5). - **OS chrome.** - **Display colour management and HDR.** macOS ColorSync versus Windows SDR sRGB and Windows HDR mode. Parity is judged on captures (§5.7). - **GPU-vendor differences.** `fract(sin)` noise, MSAA sample positions, anisotropic filtering and fp16 handling (§5.3, §5.5). ### 1.4 Out of scope | Item | Why it is out of scope | |---|---| | RealityKit renderer study (`--renderer-study`, `--realitykit`, RendererStudy.swift, 333 lines) | An Apple-only migration experiment; it does not ship. | | SceneKit shader-string GPU probes: LoadedGPUProbe (252), AOPreparationProbe (148), AOMaterialBinding (77), BenchmarkGPUCapture (39) | They depend on SceneKit modifier-text surgery and owned Metal command buffers. Replaced by per-view GPU timers, scene-feature toggles (ABBA variants become flags), RenderDoc/PIX and PresentMon. Flags keep their names where the meaning survives. | | AO fixtures (AOPreparationFixture, GroundTruthAOFixture with CryptoKit, experimental GTAO) | Mac research tools. GTAO stays an analytic reference. | | Display-link diagnostics, and the CAMetalLayer presentation-calibration app | Apple pacing paths. `--display-link-lifecycle-check` becomes `--lifecycle-check` with the same checks. | | Gamepad | The Mac build has none. | | New features; fixing the Mac's failing 10-minute 60 fps gate | The port is a parity project. The Windows gate is defined in §8.2. | | Translucent title bar; native Win32 menu bar | OS chrome. A Win32 menu also brings modal-loop and Alt/F10 problems. | | Microsoft Store, Steam, public release | They wait for legal review of four things: character copyright and trademarks (Lucasfilm/Disney, Pixar); provenance of the robot models obtained from mirrors; CERN-OHL-S-2.0 obligations; and reimplementing maths read from captures (§9). | | Pixel-identical text to SF fonts; bit-identical physics traces across OSes | Impossible because of licensing and libm. Replaced by layout and statistical parity. | | Windows UI Automation for the custom-drawn menu | SDL does not provide it. Decision item; the default is a later follow-up. | --- ## 2. Recommendation ### 2.1 Chosen strategy: seams first, same source Make the Swift game portable on the live Mac line. Then add a second, portable presentation backend that renders the same engine-neutral scene data. **Step 1: extract the game from SceneKit and AppKit.** - Small, behaviour-neutral, codemod-generated PRs move game logic and world construction out of SceneKit and AppKit: - about 2,100 lines into **GameCore**; - about 3,900 lines into **WorldBuild**. - They sit behind six narrow ports: RenderScene, Canvas2D, AudioOut, PlatformShell, Storage and TestHost. - Each PR must leave Mac SceneKit captures unchanged within the measured noise floor. **Step 2: build the portable backend:** - **SDL3 3.4.x** for windowing and input [S12]; - **bgfx** for rendering: Direct3D 11 on Windows, Metal on the Mac, Vulkan as secondary [S1]; - **Blend2D** for HUD and sign text [S15]; - **PortableMixer**, a small C mixer, on miniaudio 0.11.x [S16]. **Where the work happens.** The portable backend also runs inside the Mac app behind `--renderer bgfx`. Most fidelity work therefore happens on the reference M2, against SceneKit at the same commit. **What stays the same:** - SimulationCore (2,333 lines) and its 39 checks compile unchanged apart from `import VecMath`. - SceneKit stays the Mac default. - Moving the Mac to bgfx-Metal is an optional, measured decision at G4. ### 2.2 Why **Both judges ranked it first:** - graphics lens: 50, against 48 for own-renderer and 45 for engine; - delivery lens: 50, against 47 for engine and 44 for own-renderer. **It solves fidelity at its root.** A custom forward renderer can reproduce SceneKit's semantics directly: - fog applied before `.fragment` modifiers; - the wear-atlas multiply applied after lighting; - geometry modifiers that also run in the shadow and AO prepasses; - two world-anchored single-cascade suns; - a full-resolution AO prepass that includes the overlays; - premultiplied overlays a few millimetres apart, in SceneKit's sort order. **It keeps one source of truth.** Agents keep writing Swift on the Mac, and Windows compiles the same lines. Only presentation code exists twice, and compiler-checked mechanisms hold it in step (§6). **It delivers early and measurably.** In Scenario A (§7): - Windows CI in week 2; - the full-content stress spike in weeks 3-4; - a Windows sandbox alpha around week 10, and a race alpha around week 13; - go/no-go gates with named fallbacks. **It is moderate in size.** About 15-18k new lines, against about 25k for the own-renderer plan. bgfx has a mature D3D11 path and compiles shaders offline. It also provides: - TexCoord0-7, transient buffers and compute; - `readTexture` and per-view GPU timers; - a WARP adapter ID and a Noop renderer for GPU-less CI [S2]. **The first two phases are no-regret.** The goldens, characterisation kit, Windows CI and the GameCore/WorldBuild extraction are needed by every strategy, Godot included. ### 2.3 Alternatives considered | Alternative | Why it lost | What this plan keeps from it | |---|---|---| | **Godot 4.7.x + SwiftGodot** | Godot 4.7.2 is current [S19], but:
• With MSAA, CompositorEffects run only at POST_TRANSPARENT (godot#106743, open [S19]), so a custom AO prepass is impossible at 2x MSAA.
• The Linear tonemap clips, and adjustments run after it.
• Directional shadows share one camera-fitted atlas, so world-anchored 4096/2048 maps need an engine patch.
• `light()` replaces only the direct BRDF.
• SwiftGodot ships prebuilt binaries for Apple only, with unverified stability elsewhere [S20]. | Object-ID pass, look-reference kit, debt ledger, pinned versions, clean-VM matrix. **Fallback at G2:** Godot plus a C-ABI or godot-cpp presenter over the same data contract. It also needs Swift on Windows for the shared core. | | **Own SceneKit-shaped renderer on wgpu** | • Largest surface: about 25k lines, and codemodding all 70 app files within 4 weeks.
• Windows feedback arrives last, around week 16.

560 ## 6. Keeping in step with the fast-moving Mac line 561 562 ### 6.1 Mechanisms 563 564 1. **Single source, with honest local coverage.** 565 - `build-app.sh` also builds `MarvinPortable` and its Metal and SPIR-V shader variants on the Mac. The extra time is measured in P0 (estimate about one minute). 566 - So shared-code portability breaks, Metal-backend breaks and most logic breaks show up at the agent's desk. 567 - **D3D shaders can only be compiled on Windows** [S38], and Windows-only Swift/Foundation differences only show there. `swift-windows` CI therefore builds MarvinPortable and compiles every D3D11 shader variant on every push. 568 - Agents see those failures in CI (target under 20 minutes), not locally. 569 2. **Boundaries enforced by compiler and CI.** 570 - Shared modules build on GitHub Linux and Windows on every push. 571 - Lints allow `SCN*`, `NS*`, `MTL*` and `AV*` symbols only in Mac targets. 572 - Lints forbid new KVC uniforms, untyped shader strings outside Effects, and bare libm transcendentals in generators. 573 3. **Exhaustive enums as a feature contract.** `ShaderKind`, `MaterialFeature`, `InputAction`, `AudioRole` and `HUDElement` are switched exhaustively in both backends. The escape hatch `.parityDebt(issue:)` renders the error colour. 574 4. **Shared shader sources.** `Shaders/Effects/*.fxh` generates both backends, so most of the ~5 shader or material edits a day propagate without Windows work. 575 5. **Codemods and file leases.** 576 - Move-only, re-runnable codemods are re-run on a fresh HEAD rather than rebasing stale diffs. 577 - Hot files are leased in announced windows of about 2 hours (`docs/windows-port/leases.md`), hottest first: App.swift, then TownWorld, DirtWorld, TownSmoke. 578 6. **Same-commit goldens.** Parity always compares against SceneKit at the same SHA. 579 7. **Parity-debt ledger** (`parity/debt.json`: PR, area, views, age), mirrored to labelled issues. 580 - **Sizing from measured throughput.** 581 - 61 of the last 80 commits touched render, scene or HUD files, and 42 changed shader or material text. A per-item cap would therefore trip daily. 582 - Debt arises only when a change is not carried by the shared mechanisms: a new ShaderKind or MaterialFeature, a new pass, or a structural render change. 583 - Expected inflow is about 1-3 items a day (unverified; measured from P2). 584 - **Until G3:** the ledger is tracked and burned down by a parity lane of 0.3-0.5 FTE from about week 10. It **never blocks Mac PRs**. A weekly burn-down goes in the status note. 585 - **From G3 onward:** 586 - Debt blocks the Windows release candidate and turns the nightly red. It still never blocks Mac PRs. 587 - An item older than 10 working days, or a backlog that grows three weeks running, escalates to you, with three options: add parity capacity, waive the item, or slow Mac visual changes in that area (§11 item 5). 588 - A Windows release needs zero unwaived debt. 589 8. **Pinned versions** in `tools/versions.json`: Swift, bgfx/bx/bimg, shaderc, SDL3, Blend2D, miniaudio, CORE-MATH, PresentMon and FLIP. ### 8.2 Performance gate and budgets

**The Windows release gate (decision §11 item 4; this is the recommendation):**
1. **Gating desktop:** the existing sustained gate, unchanged.
   - Run: 603 s city roam in clear and storm, audio on, at least 1000 m driven.
   - Frame delivery: zero presented intervals over 25 ms (PresentMon MsBetweenDisplayChange); rolling 10 s ≥59.8 fps; live counter ≥59.
   - GPU: p99 ≤12.5 ms and maximum <16.667 ms.
   - Manifest: quality manifest (MSAA 2, shadow widths [2048, 4096], exploration detail on); `presentationVerified` true.
   - Headroom target at G4: GPU p99 ≤8 ms.
2. **780M tier, Mac-equivalence:** on identical 603 s clear and storm runs, each metric must be at least as good as SceneKit-on-M2 at the same commit: mean fps, count of intervals over 25 ms, minimum rolling-10 s fps, and GPU p99.
   - The Mac fails the sustained gate today: 57.23 fps mean with 1,662 gaps, and other runs at 53.0-56.4 fps. Demanding the full gate of an "M2-class" iGPU would therefore not be "same".
   - Windows measures presentation, which is stricter than the Mac's callback cadence.

**SceneKit's measured cost on the M2** (production frame, 1920x1080, 2x MSAA). This is the basis for budgets.

| Item | Measured | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Whole frame, live | GPU median 13.72, p95 15.43, p99 16.02 ms | Metal HUD, 45 s full city |
| Whole frame, frozen | 11.27-11.95 ms; vertex mean 8.47 ms and fragment mean 8.80 ms (overlapping) | owned command buffer; Metal System Trace |
| AO prepass (render encoder 3) | 20.46% of a 16.83 ms replay | docs/apple-gpu-profiling.md:322-327 |
| SSAO compute (encoder 4) | 9.95% of the replay | same |
| AO in total (SSAO off) | 4.5-5 ms saved | frozen ABBA |
| Shadows (off) | about 5 ms saved | frozen ABBA |
| Dust (hidden) | 1.0-1.15 ms saved; 9.49% of the replay | apple-gpu-profiling.md:195-204 |
| Ground overlay | 8.15% of the replay, 5.35% of it inside the AO prepass | apple-gpu-profiling.md:325-327 |
| Isolated "AO input diagnostic" | 1.40-1.64 ms. A diagnostic copy that excludes AO computation and main rendering, so **not** the production cost. | apple-gpu-profiling.md:355-363 |

ABBA deltas overlap and do not sum, and replay time is inflated against live. The frame is geometry-bound: two shadow maps, the AO prepass and the main pass each redraw the scene.

**Per-pass early-warning budgets (median ms).** These are initial hypotheses from the M2 shares above. At G0b they are replaced by P0b-measured naive costs × 1.3, which must fit under each tier's total.

| Pass group | Approximate share | Gating desktop (total ≤6.5) | 780M (total ≤13.7) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Shadow maps | 35% | ≤2.3 | ≤4.8 |
| AO prepass, SSAO and blur | 30% | ≤2.0 | ≤4.1 |
| Opaque, sky, overlays and trails | 20% | ≤1.3 | ≤2.7 |
| Particles | 8% | ≤0.5 | ≤1.1 |
| Resolve, bloom, tone map and HUD | 6% | ≤0.4 | ≤0.8 |

- FrameState diff plus bgfx submit p95 ≤2.5 ms.
- Dynamic uploads ≤0.5 ms.
- PortableMixer ≤10% of one core. On the Mac, the AVAudioEngine IO thread used about 16.9 CPU-seconds a minute.

The runner refuses to start unless all of these hold:

- **Windows HDR off**, Auto HDR off and Auto Color Management off;

entries.description:
Send files to the user. Use this for any file the user would want to see — a generated diagram, a report, a screenshot, a built artifact — and you want it surfaced, not just mentioned. Send deliverables as they are produced, not batched at the end of the task: a complete draft or a meaningfully updated version of the thing the user asked for is worth sending mid-task, so they can follow progress and redirect early. Do NOT send routine working files — scratch files, debug output, partial fragments, or every incremental save of something you're still actively editing; each call renders a file card in the conversation, and a stream of cards for one file is noise. Re-send a file only when it has meaningfully changed since the last send. Paths can be absolute or relative to the current working directory.

Add a `caption` when a one-liner of context helps ("the failing case is row 42", "before vs after"). Skip it if the file speaks for itself.

Set `status` on every call. Use `proactive` when you're initiating — the user is away and you want this to reach their phone (build artifact ready, report generated). Use `normal` when replying to something the user just said.

Set `display` to choose how the file is presented. Use `'render'` when the user should see the content inline in the side panel right now — a chart, a rendered HTML page, a diagram, an image. Use `'attach'` when the file is something they'll save and open elsewhere — source code, a spreadsheet, a document for another app — and an inline preview would just be noise. Leave it unset to let the client decide by file type.

Files must already exist on the local filesystem — the tool sends files, it doesn't fetch URLs or render content. When unsure of a path, verify with ls first; absolute paths avoid ambiguity about the working directory.

Example: SendUserFile({ files: ["report.md"], caption: "Here's the report.", status: "normal" })

files.description: File paths (absolute or relative to cwd) to send to the user. Always pass an array, even for a single file.

caption.description: Optional short caption for the file(s).

status.description: Use 'proactive' when you're surfacing a file the user hasn't asked for and needs to see now — a generated artifact, a completed report. Use 'normal' when replying to something the user just said.

display.description: How the client should present the file. 'render' opens it inline in the side panel (for HTML, SVG, Mermaid, images, PDFs — anything the user wants to look at now). 'attach' shows a download card only, no inline preview (for deliverables the user will save and open elsewhere). Omit to let the client decide by file type — today that means renderable types render and everything else attaches, same as before this parameter existed.

content.text:
I've written the plan to `docs/windows-port/plan.md` and sent you a copy. It's long, about 1,250 lines, so here's the short version. Nothing has been built or run on Windows yet; the riskiest assumptions are scheduled to be tested in the first two weeks.

**Recommendation: make the existing Swift game portable, then add a second renderer that also runs on Windows.**

- **Step 1, on the Mac version:** move the game logic and world building out of the Mac-only code in small pull requests. Each one must leave the Mac game's screenshots unchanged. The game logic only needs a small replacement for Apple's math library to compile on Windows.
- **Step 2:** build a new frontend that draws the same game data, using cross-platform open-source libraries: SDL3 for the window and input, bgfx for 3D (Direct3D 11 on Windows, Metal on the Mac), Blend2D for the HUD and text, and miniaudio for sound.
- **Mac stays on SceneKit for now.** The new renderer also runs inside the Mac app behind a flag. That lets "same graphics" be measured directly, by rendering identical scenes with both renderers on the same commit and comparing the images. Whether the Mac moves to the new renderer is a measured decision near the end.

**Why this one won:** both judges ranked it first, with a different strategy in second place for each. The three strategies compared were:

| Strategy | Why it lost |
|---|---|
| Godot game engine | Can't match several SceneKit specifics without patching the engine: the ambient-occlusion pass with anti-aliasing on, the tone curve, and the two fixed sun shadow maps. The Swift-to-Godot bridge is also unproven on Windows. Kept as a fallback if the renderer falls 3+ weeks behind. |
| Own renderer from scratch | About 25k new lines, and Windows feedback only arrives around week 16. |
| Unity / Unreal | Would mean rewriting the whole game in C# or C++. |

**Effort:** about 50 engineer-weeks with coding agents.

| Staffing | Release candidate |
|---|---|
| 3 engineers + agents | about week 24 (range 20–31) |
| 2 engineers + agents | about week 30 (range 26–38) |
| You directing agents alone | weeks 36–48, at 12+ hours a week from you |

Hardware is about $4–6k: a Windows PC with an RTX 4060, a laptop with a Mac-comparable integrated GPU, and a used M2 Mac mini for comparison tests. Code signing is $9.99 a month.

**Biggest risks:**
- **SceneKit's look may not be fully reproducible.** Its tone curve, bloom, ambient occlusion and shadow filtering aren't documented, so the plan measures them with test scenes before any shader work starts.
- **The new code paths may fall behind the Mac.** The Mac version changes 15+ times a day. Shared shader sources and compiler-checked feature lists carry most changes to both platforms automatically. The rest goes on a parity backlog that never blocks Mac work.
- **The generated town could come out differently on Windows** if math results differ slightly. A layout fingerprint is compared across macOS, Linux and Windows from week 1.
- **Your review time is a bottleneck.** You're the only reviewer, and visual sign-off per your rules depends on you.

**Decisions you need to make:** the plan lists 20, each with a recommended answer. The most important:
1. Approve this strategy.
2. Pick a staffing level.
3. **Fonts:** SF Pro, SF Mono and Avenir Next can't legally ship on Windows. The plan proposes free open-licensed fonts on both platforms, which changes the Mac HUD slightly.
4. **Windows performance bar:** the full 60 fps gate on the RTX 4060 PC, and "no worse than the Mac" on the laptop. The Mac itself fails the 10-minute 60 fps test today.
5. **No public release yet:** distribute only to named testers until a lawyer has reviewed:
   - the Star Wars and Pixar character rights;
   - where the robot models came from;
   - the open-hardware licence obligations of Marvin's model.

**First two weeks:** the decision memo and hardware orders. Then a math-library pull request with Windows/Linux CI running the game-logic tests, reference screenshots from SceneKit, and a "hello triangle" test of the new libraries rendered on GitHub's Windows runners. All of this is useful whichever strategy you choose.

## Appendix A: Corrections to the proposals' claims

| Claim | Correction |
|---|---|
| bgfx and Blend2D can ship as SE-0482 artifact bundles. | SE-0482 is limited to C libraries [S11]. Use a pinned prebuild or SwiftPM C++ targets. |
| Godot rejected because its scene graph is float32. | Irrelevant: the double-precision core stays outside any engine. The valid reasons are in §2.3. |
| P0 takes 1 engineer-week; RC in 16-17 weeks. | About 50 engineer-weeks; RC around week 24 with three engineers, around week 30 with two (§7). |
| DetMath makes the city bit-identical "by definition". | It is a hypothesis to prove with the three-OS hash, and it covers only transcendentals. Vector-maths formula order is handled by VecMath. |
| Thresholds at one third of the distance to rejected looks. | The primary anchor is at least 3× the measured per-device noise floor. Rejected looks are an upper bound. |
| Edge-map IoU for geometry. | Replaced by the object-ID pass. |
| Converge noise to an integer hash. | Replaced by the Apple-baked townNoise LUT. |
| The Windows PC is only a runner. | It is also an interactive agent workstation, under a separate account. |
| App.swift touched by 47 of 80 commits. | Git shows 49. |
| "PIX/RenderDoc programmatic capture" for D3D11. | PIX captures D3D11 only via D3D11On12 [S31]. RenderDoc is the D3D11 tool. |
| TimestampQueryInsidePasses for per-pass time; PipelineCache on D3D12 and Metal. | Not on Apple GPUs; Vulkan only [S21]. |
| Byte-identical Phase-1 goldens. | They would flake on SceneKit noise. Use the floor. |
| An 11.8 ms M2 budget. | SceneKit itself measures 13.72 ms live median and 16.02 ms p99. Budgets now come from production pass costs (§8.2). |
| Static stdlib linking supported. | Foundation linking fails in 6.4 [S8]. |
| Two suns on an 8192 atlas each get at least 4096 (Godot). | The atlas is split and camera-fitted; world anchoring needs a patch. The "shimmer" claim was overstated: Godot texel-snaps. |
| Linear tonemap plus a LUT reproduces SceneKit (Godot). | Linear clips, and adjustments run after the tonemap. |
| A custom AO pass is a fallback (Godot). | Impossible at 2x MSAA (godot#106743 [S19]). |
| SwiftGodot builds Windows libraries in CI. | Windows is source-build only [S20]. |
| Shim `simd` on both OSes (engine proposal; the previous draft rejected this for the Mac). | **Adopted, with a proof.** A pure-Swift VecMath that follows Apple's header formulas runs on all OSes, the Mac included. Bit-equality against Apple simd is proved on the Mac. Re-exporting Apple simd on the Mac only would leave the generators' simd-based threshold tests platform-dependent. |
| Instance uniforms for coating and walkers (Godot). | Limited to 16 per shader, with no `mat4`. |
| Diligent's Metal backend "reported" commercial-only. | Verified: commercial licence [S41]. |

files['tools/sync-assets.py']='''#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Copy the macOS simulator's runtime assets into assets/ (gitignored).

The macOS game is the reference and is never modified. Generated assets
(Marvin geometry.bin, BB8/WallE Generated/) are gitignored there, so by default
they are read from the main checkout; override with MARVIN_MAC_RESOURCES.
Run apps/simulator-macos/build-app.sh first if they are missing.
"""
import os, shutil, subprocess, sys
from pathlib import Path

root = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
def main_checkout():
    common = subprocess.run(["git", "rev-parse", "--path-format=absolute", "--git-common-dir"],
                            cwd=root, capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.strip()
    return Path(common).parent if common else root.parent.parent
src = Path(os.environ.get("MARVIN_MAC_RESOURCES", main_checkout() / "apps/simulator-macos/Resources"))
dst = root / "assets"
SKIP_SUFFIX = {".zip", ".glb", ".hdr", ".rtf", ".icns"}
FOLDERS = ["Marvin", "R2D2", "BB8", "WallE", "City", "Dirt", "Audio", "Icons"]
TEXTURE_IMPORT = """[remap]

importer="texture"
type="CompressedTexture2D"

[params]

compress/mode=0
mipmaps/generate=true
"""

if not (src / "Marvin/geometry.bin").exists():
    sys.exit(f"missing {src}/Marvin/geometry.bin - run apps/simulator-macos/build-app.sh in the main checkout")
copied = 0
for folder in FOLDERS:
    for path in (src / folder).rglob("*"):
        if path.is_dir() or path.suffix.lower() in SKIP_SUFFIX:
            continue
        target = dst / path.relative_to(src)
        target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        if not target.exists() or target.stat().st_mtime < path.stat().st_mtime or target.stat().st_size != path.stat().st_size:
            shutil.copy2(path, target)
            copied += 1
        if path.suffix.lower() in {".jpg", ".png"}:
            imp = target.with_name(target.name + ".import")
            if not imp.exists():
                imp.write_text(TEXTURE_IMPORT)
print(f"assets: {copied} files updated from {src}")
'''
for k,v in files.items():
    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(k) or '.', exist_ok=True); open(k,'w').write(v)
for k in ['tools/godot','tools/build','tools/checks','tools/sync-assets.py']: os.chmod(k,0o755)

# Marvin Simulator: Godot port

A faithful port of the macOS game in `apps/simulator-macos` to Godot 4.7 (.NET/C#), so it runs on Windows as well as macOS. The goal is that it looks and plays as close to the macOS game as possible.

**The macOS game is the reference, not a dependency.** Never modify anything under `apps/simulator-macos`. Read it, run it, capture it, and compare against it.

## Layout

| Path | Contents |
|---|---|
| `project.godot`, `MarvinGodot.csproj` | Godot project (Forward+, C#). Assembly `MarvinGodot`. |
| `src/Core/` | `MarvinCore`: a C# port of `Sources/SimulationCore`. Pure C#, no Godot types, double precision. One `.cs` file per Swift file, same file names. |
| `src/Checks/` | `MarvinChecks`: a console port of `Tests/SimulationCoreTests` (SimulationChecks). Runs without Godot. |
| `scripts/` | Godot-side C# for the app target, mirroring `Sources/MarvinSimulator` file by file (e.g. `scripts/World/DirtWorld.cs`, `scripts/Town/TownWorld.cs`). |
| `shaders/` | `.gdshader` ports of the SceneKit shader modifiers. |
| `scenes/` | Godot scenes. `Main.tscn` is the entry point. |
| `assets/` | **Gitignored.** Runtime assets copied from the macOS game by `tools/sync-assets.py`. |
| `reference/` | **Gitignored.** Reference outputs from the macOS game (SimulationChecks output, captures). |
| `tools/` | `env.sh`, `godot`, `build`, `checks`, `sync-assets.py`. |

## Build and run

```sh
apps/simulator-godot/tools/sync-assets.py      # once, and after macOS assets change
apps/simulator-godot/tools/build               # dotnet build (Godot assembly + MarvinCore)
apps/simulator-godot/tools/checks              # SimulationChecks port (no Godot)
apps/simulator-godot/tools/godot --headless --import   # first time: import assets
apps/simulator-godot/tools/godot               # run the game
apps/simulator-godot/tools/godot -- <game args> # game arguments go after "--" (OS.GetCmdlineUserArgs)
```

`tools/env.sh` sets `DOTNET_ROOT` (`~/.dotnet`) and `GODOT` (`~/Applications/Godot_mono.app`). In this shell, `cat` and `ls` are aliased to missing tools: use `command cat`, `command ls`, or the Read and Write tools. Use `gtimeout` (GNU coreutils) to bound any Godot run.

## Translation rules

**Mirror the Swift code.** Port file by file and keep every type, member and function name **verbatim**, including Swift's camelCase member names. Do not restructure, "improve" or simplify behaviour. If something cannot be mirrored, note the deviation in a `// PORT:` comment.

**Numbers.**
- Swift `Double` → `double`, `Float` → `float`, `CGFloat` → `double`.
- Swift `Int` is 64-bit. Use `long` wherever values can exceed 32 bits: hashes, seeds, RNG state, products of indices. Plain `int` is fine for small counts and indices.
- Wrapping operators `&+ &- &*` → C#'s default unchecked arithmetic on the same width. Bit shifts on unsigned types → the same unsigned C# types.
- `x.rounded()` is round-half-away-from-zero: `Math.Round(x, MidpointRounding.AwayFromZero)`. C#'s default `Math.Round` is banker's rounding and is **wrong** here. `.rounded(.down)` → `Math.Floor`, `.rounded(.up)` → `Math.Ceiling`, `.rounded(.towardZero)` → `Math.Truncate`.
- `Int(x)` truncates toward zero: `(long)x`. `truncatingRemainder(dividingBy:)` → `%` on doubles. `%` on integers is truncated in both languages.
- `Float` maths uses the float functions (`MathF.Sin`), `Double` maths uses `Math.Sin`. On macOS .NET calls the same Darwin libm as Swift, so results should be bit-identical. Keep operation order exactly as written; do not use FMA.

**simd.** Core provides `Double2`, `Double3`, `Double4`, `Float2`, `Float3`, `Float4`, `QuatD`, `QuatF`, `Double3x3` and `Float4x4`, plus a static `Simd` class mirroring Apple's functions (`Simd.dot`, `Simd.length`, `Simd.length_squared`, `Simd.distance`, `Simd.normalize`, `Simd.cross`, `Simd.min`, `Simd.max`, `Simd.mix`, `Simd.clamp`, quaternion `act` and `slerp`). They follow Apple's header formulas:
- `dot` sums the lane products left to right;
- `length = sqrt(dot(x, x))`;
- `normalize(x) = x * (1 / sqrt(dot(x, x)))`;
- `distance = length(x - y)`.

**Value semantics.** Swift structs **and Swift arrays/dictionaries** are values; copying one and mutating the copy never affects the original. C# arrays and `List<T>` are references. Where Swift copies a struct that holds arrays (for example `var stopped = state; stopped.stop()`) and then mutates either side, the C# port must deep-copy, or the mutation leaks. Port value-type models as C# `struct`s with explicit `Clone()`/copy where they hold collections, and audit every copy site.

**Randomness.** Seeded generators (custom `RandomNumberGenerator` structs, LCGs, hashes) must give identical sequences. Swift's `Double.random(in:using:)`, `Float.random(in:using:)`, `Int.random(in:using:)`, `Bool.random(using:)` and `shuffle(using:)` / `shuffled(using:)` / `randomElement(using:)` have specific stdlib algorithms. Port them **exactly**, from the Swift stdlib source, into `Marvin.Core.SwiftRandom`. Unseeded calls (`SystemRandomNumberGenerator`, plain `.random(in:)`) may use `System.Random.Shared`.

**Collections.** Swift `Dictionary`/`Set` iteration order is unspecified. Where Swift code depends on iteration order, the result was already nondeterministic: keep the C# behaviour deterministic and note it.

## SceneKit → Godot

Coordinate systems match: right-handed, +Y up, cameras look down −Z, metres.

| SceneKit | Godot |
|---|---|
| `SCNNode` without geometry | `Node3D` |
| `SCNNode` with geometry | `MeshInstance3D` (or a `Node3D` with a `MeshInstance3D` child when the node also has children with their own transforms) |
| `position`, `scale` | `Position`, `Scale` |
| `eulerAngles` (pitch, yaw, roll) | Set `RotationOrder = EulerOrder.Zyx` and `Rotation = euler`, or build `Basis.FromEuler(euler, EulerOrder.Zyx)`. **Measured:** SceneKit's matrix equals Godot's ZYX basis. Godot's default YXZ order is wrong. |
| `simdOrientation` / quaternion | `Quaternion` (x, y, z, w) |
| `pivot` (translation-only, measured) | A point q maps to `position + R·q − pivotTranslation`. Used only in TownShadowBatch and World.swift. Re-measure with a SceneKit script for anything else. |
| `isHidden` | `Visible = false` |
| `opacity` | `GeometryInstance3D.Transparency = 1 - opacity` |
| `castsShadow` | `CastShadow` |
| Shadow-only proxy via `categoryBitMask` | `CastShadow = ShadowCastingSetting.ShadowsOnly` |
| `renderingOrder` | `Material.RenderPriority` (sorting among transparents); opaque order is by depth |
| `SCNLevelOfDetail(worldSpaceDistance:)` | One `MeshInstance3D` per level with `VisibilityRangeBegin`/`End` |
| `SCNGeometrySource`/`Element` | `ArrayMesh.AddSurfaceFromArrays`. Godot has `UV`, `UV2` and `CUSTOM0`-`CUSTOM3` (up to 4 floats each, `ArrayFormat.FormatCustomRgbaFloat`) for extra channels, plus `Color`. |
| Triangle winding | **SceneKit front faces are counter-clockwise, Godot's are clockwise.** Reverse each triangle's index order when converting (or the faces are culled). |
| `SCNBox`/`SCNSphere`/`SCNCylinder`/`SCNPlane`/`SCNFloor` | `BoxMesh`/`SphereMesh`/`CylinderMesh`/`PlaneMesh`, or generate the same tessellation in code. Match segment counts and chamfers. |
| `SCNMaterial` `.physicallyBased` | `StandardMaterial3D` (metallic/roughness) or a `ShaderMaterial` |
| `.lambert` / `.constant` | Diffuse-only shading / `ShadingMode.Unshaded` |
| `diffuse` colour (sRGB `NSColor`) | Albedo `Color` (Godot colours are sRGB; it linearises them) |
| Shader modifier `.geometry` | `vertex()` in a `.gdshader` |
| `.surface` | `fragment()` (set ALBEDO, ROUGHNESS, METALLIC, NORMAL_MAP, EMISSION, ...) |
| `.fragment` (post-lighting colour) | No direct hook. Reproduce the effect inside `fragment()`/`light()`, or `render_mode unshaded` with manual lighting. Choose whichever matches the captures best and document it. |
| `SCNLight` `.directional` | `DirectionalLight3D`. SceneKit intensity 1000 ≈ Godot `LightEnergy` 1.0 (calibrate against captures). |
| `.ambient` | `Environment.AmbientLight*` |
| Shadow map size | Project setting `rendering/lights_and_shadows/directional_shadow/size` (one atlas shared by all directional lights) |
| `SCNCamera.fieldOfView` (vertical) | `Camera3D.Fov` (vertical with `KeepAspect = Height`); same `Near`/`Far` |
| `wantsHDR`, exposure, bloom | `Environment` tonemap (Linear or Filmic, chosen by capture comparison), exposure, Glow |
| `screenSpaceAmbientOcclusion*` | `Environment.Ssao*` |
| Scene fog (linear start/end) | `Environment` fog in depth mode (`FogMode = Depth`, begin/end, curve 1.0 for linear) |
| `lightingEnvironment` (IBL image) | `Environment` sky (`PanoramaSkyMaterial` or a sky shader), ambient and reflections from the sky |
| `background` colour | `Environment.BackgroundMode = Color` |
| `SCNView.antialiasingMode` | `Viewport.Msaa3D` |
| AppKit views, Quartz drawing | `Control` nodes; immediate-mode drawing in `_Draw()` |
| SF Pro / SF Mono | `SystemFont` with `FontNames` `["SF Pro Text", "SF Pro", ".AppleSystemUIFont"]` / `["SF Mono", "Menlo"]`; on Windows it falls back to Segoe UI / Consolas |
| `NSEvent.keyCode` | `InputEventKey.PhysicalKeycode` |
| `Timer` 1/60 s tick | `_Process(delta)`, with the same dt clamping and pause rules |
| UserDefaults / Application Support | `user://` (`ConfigFile` for settings, JSON for scores) |
| GCD background world build | `Task.Run` for data generation; node-tree changes on the main thread |
| AVAudioEngine | Godot audio buses and `AudioStreamPlayer`s (or an `AudioStreamGenerator` mixer), keeping gains, rates, pans and filters |

**Assets.** Load from `res://assets/...`. Marvin's `geometry.bin` and the JSON meshes are raw files read with `FileAccess`. Textures are imported with mipmaps (sync writes `.import` files).

## Validation

- **Logic:** `tools/checks` must print the same values as `reference/simulation-checks-swift.txt`, the macOS SimulationChecks output at the same commit. On macOS the numbers should match exactly.
- **Visuals:** compare captures of the same scene, camera and state against the macOS game's captures. Run the macOS game's own capture modes (`'apps/simulator-macos/.build/Marvin Simulator.app/Contents/MacOS/MarvinSimulator' --smoke-test DIR`, `--town-smoke-test DIR` and others; see its README) and add matching capture modes to the Godot game (`tools/godot -- --capture <name> DIR`). Inspect both images side by side. A passing number is never visual acceptance.
- **Behaviour:** port the macOS smoke checks that verify gameplay, and keep their JSON report keys.

## Agent rules

- Do not modify `apps/simulator-macos` (or anything outside `apps/simulator-godot`).
- Do not commit or push. The orchestrator commits.
- Stay inside your assigned files and folders. Report every deviation from the macOS behaviour or look, and anything you could not port.

# Marvin Simulator: Godot port

A faithful port of the macOS game in `apps/simulator-macos` to Godot 4.7 (.NET/C#), so it runs on Windows as well as macOS. The goal is that it looks and plays as close to the macOS game as possible.

**The macOS game is the reference, not a dependency.** Never modify anything under `apps/simulator-macos`. Read it, run it, capture it, and compare against it.

## Layout

| Path | Contents |
|---|---|
| `project.godot`, `MarvinGodot.csproj` | Godot project (Forward+, C#). Assembly `MarvinGodot`. |
| `src/Core/` | `MarvinCore`: a C# port of `Sources/SimulationCore`. Pure C#, no Godot types, double precision. One `.cs` file per Swift file, same file names. |
| `src/Checks/` | `MarvinChecks`: a console port of `Tests/SimulationCoreTests` (SimulationChecks). Runs without Godot. |
| `scripts/` | Godot-side C# for the app target, mirroring `Sources/MarvinSimulator` file by file (e.g. `scripts/World/DirtWorld.cs`, `scripts/Town/TownWorld.cs`). |
| `shaders/` | `.gdshader` ports of the SceneKit shader modifiers. |
| `scenes/` | Godot scenes. `Main.tscn` is the entry point. |
| `assets/` | **Gitignored.** Runtime assets copied from the macOS game by `tools/sync-assets.py`. |
| `reference/` | **Gitignored.** Reference outputs from the macOS game (SimulationChecks output, captures). |
| `tools/` | `env.sh`, `godot`, `build`, `checks`, `sync-assets.py`. |

## Build and run

```sh
apps/simulator-godot/tools/sync-assets.py      # once, and after macOS assets change
apps/simulator-godot/tools/build               # dotnet build (Godot assembly + MarvinCore)
apps/simulator-godot/tools/checks              # SimulationChecks port (no Godot)
apps/simulator-godot/tools/godot --headless --import   # first time: import assets
apps/simulator-godot/tools/godot               # run the game
apps/simulator-godot/tools/godot -- <game args> # game arguments go after "--" (OS.GetCmdlineUserArgs)
```

`tools/env.sh` sets `DOTNET_ROOT` (`~/.dotnet`) and `GODOT` (`~/Applications/Godot_mono.app`). In this shell, `cat` and `ls` are aliased to missing tools: use `command cat`, `command ls`, or the Read and Write tools. Use `gtimeout` (GNU coreutils) to bound any Godot run.

## Translation rules

**Mirror the Swift code.** Port file by file and keep every type, member and function name **verbatim**, including Swift's camelCase member names. Do not restructure, "improve" or simplify behaviour. If something cannot be mirrored, note the deviation in a `// PORT:` comment.

**Numbers.**
- Swift `Double` → `double`, `Float` → `float`, `CGFloat` → `double`.
- Swift `Int` is 64-bit. Use `long` wherever values can exceed 32 bits: hashes, seeds, RNG state, products of indices. Plain `int` is fine for small counts and indices.
- Wrapping operators `&+ &- &*` → C#'s default unchecked arithmetic on the same width. Bit shifts on unsigned types → the same unsigned C# types.
- `x.rounded()` is round-half-away-from-zero: `Math.Round(x, MidpointRounding.AwayFromZero)`. C#'s default `Math.Round` is banker's rounding and is **wrong** here. `.rounded(.down)` → `Math.Floor`, `.rounded(.up)` → `Math.Ceiling`, `.rounded(.towardZero)` → `Math.Truncate`.
- `Int(x)` truncates toward zero: `(long)x`. `truncatingRemainder(dividingBy:)` → `%` on doubles. `%` on integers is truncated in both languages.
- `Float` maths uses the float functions (`MathF.Sin`), `Double` maths uses `Math.Sin`. On macOS .NET calls the same Darwin libm as Swift, so results should be bit-identical. Keep operation order exactly as written; do not use FMA.

**simd.** Core provides `Double2`, `Double3`, `Double4`, `Float2`, `Float3`, `Float4`, `QuatD`, `QuatF`, `Double3x3` and `Float4x4`, plus a static `Simd` class mirroring Apple's functions (`Simd.dot`, `Simd.length`, `Simd.length_squared`, `Simd.distance`, `Simd.normalize`, `Simd.cross`, `Simd.min`, `Simd.max`, `Simd.mix`, `Simd.clamp`, quaternion `act` and `slerp`). They follow Apple's header formulas:
- `dot` sums the lane products left to right;
- `length = sqrt(dot(x, x))`;
- `normalize(x) = x * (1 / sqrt(dot(x, x)))`;
- `distance = length(x - y)`.

**Value semantics.** Swift structs **and Swift arrays/dictionaries** are values; copying one and mutating the copy never affects the original. C# arrays and `List<T>` are references. Where Swift copies a struct that holds arrays (for example `var stopped = state; stopped.stop()`) and then mutates either side, the C# port must deep-copy, or the mutation leaks. Port value-type models as C# `struct`s with explicit `Clone()`/copy where they hold collections, and audit every copy site.

**Randomness.** Seeded generators (custom `RandomNumberGenerator` structs, LCGs, hashes) must give identical sequences. Swift's `Double.random(in:using:)`, `Float.random(in:using:)`, `Int.random(in:using:)`, `Bool.random(using:)` and `shuffle(using:)` / `shuffled(using:)` / `randomElement(using:)` have specific stdlib algorithms. Port them **exactly**, from the Swift stdlib source, into `Marvin.Core.SwiftRandom`. Unseeded calls (`SystemRandomNumberGenerator`, plain `.random(in:)`) may use `System.Random.Shared`.

**Collections.** Swift `Dictionary`/`Set` iteration order is unspecified. Where Swift code depends on iteration order, the result was already nondeterministic: keep the C# behaviour deterministic and note it.

| `SCNNode` without geometry | `Node3D` |
| `SCNNode` with geometry | `MeshInstance3D` (or a `Node3D` with a `MeshInstance3D` child when the node also has children with their own transforms) |
| `position`, `scale` | `Position`, `Scale` |
| `eulerAngles` (pitch, yaw, roll) | Set `RotationOrder = EulerOrder.Zyx` and `Rotation = euler`, or build `Basis.FromEuler(euler, EulerOrder.Zyx)`. **Measured:** SceneKit's matrix equals Godot's ZYX basis. Godot's default YXZ order is wrong. |
| `simdOrientation` / quaternion | `Quaternion` (x, y, z, w) |

export const meta = {
  name: 'godot-port-scenekit-facade',
  description: 'Build a SceneKit-API facade over Godot for the Marvin port, calibrated against real SceneKit renders',
  phases: [
    { title: 'Facade', detail: 'SceneKit-named C# types over Godot + shader composer' },
    { title: 'Calibrate', detail: 'identical test scenes in SceneKit and Godot; tune until they match' },
  ],
}

const BASE = `Repository /Users/m1/marvin. We are porting the macOS game apps/simulator-macos (Swift, SceneKit, AppKit) to Godot 4.7 .NET (C#) in apps/simulator-godot. You are working in an ISOLATED GIT WORKTREE of the repo: do all work in the apps/simulator-godot folder OF YOUR WORKTREE (your current working directory's repo), not in /Users/m1/marvin. In the worktree first run apps/simulator-godot/tools/sync-assets.py (copies assets from the main checkout) and apps/simulator-godot/tools/godot --headless --import. READ apps/simulator-godot/PORTING.md first and follow it. Shell quirks: 'cat'/'ls' are aliased to missing tools - use 'command cat', 'command ls' or the Read tool; bound every Godot run with gtimeout. Never modify apps/simulator-macos. A parallel agent is porting SimulationCore into src/Core in the MAIN checkout; in your worktree src/Core is a placeholder - do NOT depend on it or touch src/. When done, COMMIT your work in the worktree (git add apps/simulator-godot; git commit -m "..."), do not push.`

const REPORT = {
  type: 'object',
  properties: {
    summary: { type: 'string' },
    worktree_path: { type: 'string' },
    branch: { type: 'string' },
    commit: { type: 'string' },
    api_coverage: { type: 'string', description: 'Which SceneKit/AppKit members used by Sources/MarvinSimulator are implemented, and which are not' },
    calibration: { type: 'string', description: 'What was compared, measured differences, chosen parameters (light energy scale, tonemap, exposure, ambient, shadow settings, fog)' },
    deviations: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } },
    open_issues: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } },
  },
  required: ['summary', 'worktree_path', 'branch', 'commit', 'api_coverage', 'calibration', 'deviations', 'open_issues'],
}

phase('Facade')
const facade = await agent(`${BASE}

GOAL: make porting the 13k lines of apps/simulator-macos/Sources/MarvinSimulator to C# as mechanical as possible, and centralise the "make it look like SceneKit" work, by building a SceneKit-API FACADE over Godot in apps/simulator-godot/scripts/SceneKit/ (namespace Marvin.SceneKit). Types are named exactly like SceneKit/AppKit types and members exactly like the Swift members, so Swift code like
  let node = SCNNode(geometry: g); node.position = SCNVector3(1,2,3); node.eulerAngles.y = a; node.castsShadow = false; parent.addChildNode(node)
translates to near-identical C# (new SCNNode(g); node.position = new SCNVector3(1,2,3); ...).

Scope - enumerate the ACTUAL API surface used: grep all of Sources/MarvinSimulator (ignore *Smoke.swift, *Probe.swift, RendererStudy.swift, BenchmarkGPUCapture.swift, AOMaterialBinding.swift only where they are diagnostics) for SCN*, NSColor, NSImage/CGImage/NSBitmapImageRep texture creation, simd transforms on nodes (simdPosition, simdTransform, simdWorldTransform, simdOrientation, simdWorldFront, convertPosition...), and implement every used member. The completeness critic's symbol counts are in apps/simulator-godot/docs/macos-inventory.json (key critic.api_symbol_counts) and per-subsystem fidelity specs are in the same file. At least:
- SCNVector3/SCNVector4/SCNMatrix4 (+ SCNMatrix4MakeTranslation etc. used) as structs with lowercase x/y/z/w, double constructors, conversions to Godot Vector3/Transform3D and to Marvin core doubles later (keep conversion helpers generic).
- SCNNode : Node3D (partial class; geometry via an internal MeshInstance3D child or self-managed; childNodes, addChildNode, removeFromParentNode, name, position, eulerAngles (SceneKit = Godot EulerOrder.Zyx, measured), orientation/simdOrientation, scale, pivot (measured semantics in PORTING.md - re-verify), transform/worldTransform/simd*, isHidden, opacity, castsShadow, categoryBitMask (shadow-only proxies), renderingOrder, constraints used (SCNBillboardConstraint, SCNTransformConstraint), light, camera, presentation (identity), convertPosition/convertVector, childNode(withName:recursively:), enumerateChildNodes, boundingBox, clone/flattenedClone if used.
- SCNGeometry + SCNGeometrySource/SCNGeometryElement with every initialiser used (arrays, Data with stride/offset/bytesPerComponent, MTLBuffer-backed sources -> equivalent), semantics vertex/normal/tangent/color/texcoord with mappingChannel. Pack texcoord channels deterministically: channel 0 -> UV, 1 -> UV2, 2..7 -> CUSTOM0..CUSTOM2 (two vec2 per CUSTOM, RGBA float), document it. CONVERT WINDING (SceneKit CCW front faces vs Godot CW). Multiple elements -> multiple surfaces with geometry.materials (SceneKit repeats materials cyclically if fewer than elements). levelsOfDetail (SCNLevelOfDetail worldSpaceDistance -> visibility ranges), boundingBox, firstMaterial, materials. Primitive geometries used: SCNBox (with chamferRadius and segment counts), SCNSphere, SCNCylinder, SCNPlane, SCNFloor, SCNShape (NSBezierPath extrusion), SCNText (if used) - tessellate like SceneKit (match segment counts; texture coordinates).
- SCNMaterial + SCNMaterialProperty (contents: NSColor, NSImage/CGImage/image data, MTLTexture-equivalent, float; intensity, contentsTransform, wrapS/wrapT, minification/magnification/mipFilter, maxAnisotropy, mappingChannel), lightingModel (.physicallyBased/.blinn/.phong/.lambert/.constant), diffuse/normal/roughness/metalness/emission/multiply/ambientOcclusion/transparent/specular as used, isDoubleSided, cullMode, blendMode, transparencyMode (.aOne etc.), writesToDepthBuffer, readsFromDepthBuffer, colorBufferWriteMask, transparency, shaderModifiers, setValue(forKey:) shader arguments, copy(). Implement a SHADER COMPOSER: each SCNMaterial compiles to a Godot ShaderMaterial (cache by configuration) built from a template that emulates SceneKit's material pipeline as closely as possible (PBR via Godot lighting; lambert = diffuse only; constant = unshaded; multiply applied after lighting where possible; premultiplied/aOne transparency; depth flags; cull). shaderModifiers take GODOT SHADING LANGUAGE snippets for entry points .geometry/.surface/.fragment/.lightingModel with a documented variable mapping (e.g. _geometry.position -> VERTEX, _surface.diffuse -> ALBEDO/ALPHA, _surface.position (view space) -> VERTEX in fragment, _output.color -> final colour emulation, scn_frame.inverseViewTransform -> INV_VIEW_MATRIX, scn_node.modelTransform -> MODEL_MATRIX, u_time -> TIME, texcoord channels, #pragma arguments -> uniforms set via setValue(forKey:), #pragma transparent -> blend, discard_fragment() -> discard). Translate every MSL snippet in the codebase? NO - other agents will translate each modifier when porting its file; you provide the mechanism plus a written translation guide (append a 'SceneKit facade' section to PORTING.md) and translate 2-3 representative modifiers as worked examples (e.g. BinarySky sky dome, TownGround ground overlay, DirtTrail ink) in the guide.
- SCNLight (directional/ambient/omni/spot as used: intensity, temperature, color, castsShadow, shadowMapSize, shadowSampleCount, shadowRadius, shadowColor, shadowMode forward/deferred, orthographicScale, zNear/zFar, shadowBias, automaticallyAdjustsShadowProjection, maximumShadowDistance, shadowCascadeCount, categoryBitMask) -> DirectionalLight3D/WorldEnvironment ambient etc.
- SCNCamera (fieldOfView, zNear, zFar, wantsHDR, exposureOffset, averageGray, white point, minimum/maximumExposure, wantsExposureAdaptation, bloomIntensity/Threshold/BlurRadius, screenSpaceAmbientOcclusionIntensity/Radius/Bias/DepthThreshold/NormalThreshold, usesOrthographicProjection, orthographicScale, motion blur/vignette/colour if used) -> Camera3D + Environment/CameraAttributes.
- SCNScene (rootNode, background.contents, lightingEnvironment.contents/intensity, fogStartDistance/fogEndDistance/fogColor/fogDensityExponent) -> WorldEnvironment.
- SCNView facade (scene, pointOfView, antialiasingMode, preferredFramesPerSecond, rendersContinuously, isPlaying, backgroundColor, prepare(_:), snapshot(), projectPoint/unprojectPoint, hitTest as used, isNode(insideFrustumOf:), nodesInsideFrustum) over a Godot Viewport/SubViewport; MSAA, HDR, debug options as used.
- SCNTransaction (begin/commit/disableActions/animationDuration - no-op or immediate), NSColor (sRGB/calibrated/deviceRGB constructors used, components), NSImage/NSBitmapImageRep/CGImage -> Godot Image/ImageTexture helpers for procedural textures used by the code.
Build a test/demo capture mode: 'tools/godot -- --facade-test DIR' that renders a few scenes using only the facade and saves PNGs, and exits.
Must compile cleanly with tools/build. Commit in the worktree.`,
  { label: 'scenekit-facade', phase: 'Facade', schema: REPORT, isolation: 'worktree' })

phase('Calibrate')
const calib = await agent(`${BASE}

A previous agent built the SceneKit facade in apps/simulator-godot/scripts/SceneKit/ and committed it in its worktree. Its report: ${JSON.stringify(facade)}
Work in THAT worktree (path ${facade ? facade.worktree_path : 'unknown'}, branch ${facade ? facade.branch : 'unknown'}) - cd there; do not create another worktree.

GOAL: CALIBRATE the facade so identical scenes look the same in SceneKit and Godot. Method:
1. Write small Swift scripts (in a temp dir under /private/tmp/claude-501/, NOT in the repo) that build reference scenes with real SceneKit and render them offscreen with SCNRenderer.snapshot at 1280x820 to PNG, mirroring the game's real settings: (a) race setup - two directional suns with forward shadows (4096/2048, ortho 58, sample count/radius/bias as in BinarySky.swift), ambient light, a 64x32 procedural lightingEnvironment probe like BinarySky's, linear fog 115-240, HDR camera with fixed exposure, bloom 0.38/1.2/12, SSAO 0.70/1.6/0.025, 2x MSAA, FOV/zNear/zFar as the race camera in App.swift; (b) sandbox setup per World.swift (LDR, 4x MSAA, fog 15-38, deferred shadow sun 4096); (c) menu portrait per MainMenu.swift. Put a set of test objects in each: PBR spheres across roughness/metalness, a textured ground plane using assets/Dirt or City scans, a box with chamfer, an emissive patch, a transparent premultiplied overlay, vertex-coloured mesh, and shadows falling on the ground.
2. Build the SAME scenes with the facade in C# (capture mode e.g. 'tools/godot -- --calibration DIR'), same camera, same size.
3. Compare image pairs (look at them with the Read tool; also compute per-image mean luminance/colour and simple diffs with Python+Pillow if available, or numpy). Tune the facade's mapping centrally: light energy scale, light colour/temperature handling, ambient and IBL intensity, tonemapper choice and exposure (SceneKit HDR -> which Godot tonemap/exposure/white best matches), glow parameters for bloom, SSAO parameters, shadow bias/blur/filter quality/atlas size, fog curve, sRGB/linear handling of vertex colours and NSColor variants, roughness/metalness response. Iterate until the pairs are visually very close; report residual differences honestly.

I calibrated the SceneKit facade against real SceneKit renders of the game's race, sandbox and menu setups, and committed it in the worktree as b5899d3 (not pushed).

Method: a Swift script built six 1280x820 scenes and rendered them with SCNRenderer.snapshot. The new `tools/godot -- --calibration DIR` mode builds the same scenes through the facade. The scenes mirror BinarySky (midday and evening), the sandbox in World.swift and the MainMenu portrait. Every scene contains Marvin's actual CAD model with the game's materials, PBR spheres across roughness and metalness, the Dirt clay and City scans, a vertex-tinted house, a vertex-colour banner, emissive patches, ground-tint overlays, a translucent pane, and objects casting shadows. Where whole images couldn't explain a difference, I ran small matching experiments in both renderers (self-shadowing, penumbra width, transparency per lighting model, mirror reflections).

Results, mean difference out of 255, before → after:
- race midday, chase camera: 1.90 → 1.14
- race midday, overview: 0.69 → 0.75 (slightly worse only because SceneKit draws shadow acne stripes on house walls there and Godot no longer does)
- race evening, chase camera: 1.94 → 1.78
- sandbox, orbit: 2.82 → 2.26
- sandbox, overview: 0.81 → 0.33
- menu portrait: 0.57 → 0.29

The previous agent's 64 px probe suite still holds: 101 of 109 probes are exact or within one 8-bit step.

Main corrections:
- **Deferred shadows (sandbox, menu):** modelled exactly. SceneKit le

+- **Defaults**: `SCNMaterial()` is `.blinn`, diffuse white, specular black, mipFilter `.nearest`, wrap `.clamp`; a new `SCNGeometry` has one default material. `SCNLight()` is omni 1000, `castsShadow` false, shadowRadius 3, shadowBias 1, orthographicScale 1, maximumShadowDistance 100. `SCNCamera()` fov 60 (vertical), zNear 1, zFar 100, `wantsExposureAdaptation` true, bloomThreshold 0.5, bloomBlurRadius 4. `SCNNode` castsShadow true, categoryBitMask 1.

A transparent PBR surface keeps its full specular highlight (glass-like), and `.physicallyBased` materials **ignore `transparency`** in the default `.aOne` mode (measured: opaque result). A geometry's elements are drawn in order with depth writes, so a double-sided transparent box shows only the face drawn first.
+- **No normal source**: lit as if the model-space normal were +Z.

+- **Lighting**: directional 1000 lm = irradiance 1 (Lambert, no 1/π) plus GGX specular (F0 0.04, exact height-correlated Smith visibility, no multi-scatter energy compensation). Ambient lights add albedo x intensity/1000 for every lit model, independent of metalness and without specular; `.constant` ignores them. `lightingEnvironment` diffuse and specular follow SceneKit's own roughness responses (fitted); reflections are sharp on smooth materials (the game's sky probe shows a hard horizon line in a chrome sphere) and the reflected intensity scales with f0 (no multi-scatter energy compensation, as for direct light). `.emission` adds after lighting; `.multiply` multiplies the lit colour (`mix(1, m, intensity)`).

content.text:
The groundwork is done and committed locally (5 commits, not pushed). The five parallel port streams are now running.

**Done and verified:**
- **Game logic in C#:** the 20 core files and all 39 checks. Running the checks gives output identical to the Swift version character for character, every number included. Three subtle translation bugs were found and fixed on the way.
- **SceneKit compatibility layer:** about 7,300 lines that let the Swift app code translate almost line for line. It's calibrated against real SceneKit renders of race, sandbox and menu test scenes; in the side-by-side above, SceneKit and Godot are hard to tell apart.
- **Reference material:** screenshots from 8 of the Mac game's test modes, to compare each ported part against.

**Running now, each stream in its own git worktree:**
1. Robots and sandbox
2. Race world and effects: track, sky, dunes, trails, deformable sand, sandstorm
3. Town: generator in two parts, then crowds and residents. The generated town must come out identical to the Mac one: 497 buildings, 282 people.
4. Audio: the mixer plus the Mac version's 61 audio checks
5. Interface: menu, HUD, map, loading screen

Each stream ports its files, adds capture modes matching the Mac game's, and compares its screenshots with the Mac ones until they match. After that I merge the streams, wire up the main game loop, and compare the whole game side by side.

===== audio:1
I ported RaceAudio.swift, RaceVoiceDirector.swift, RaceVoiceChecks.swift and RaceAudioSmoke.swift to scripts/Audio/. The C# follows the Swift almost line for line, on top of a new AVFoundation facade in scripts/SceneKit/.

The facade is a sample-accurate C# mixer. I wrote Swift probes that render AVAudioEngine offline on macOS 27 and fitted the facade to them:
- **Mixing:** each source's volume and pan apply at the downstream mixer input, even through the varispeed and EQ. Pan is a balance law. Each channel's gain moves towards its target by 1/1200 per frame, and the first render snaps to the target. A stopped player wired straight into the mixer keeps its last gain. outputVolume changes ramp over one render.
- **Varispeed:** a new rate applies from the next render, with a 48-input-frame delay. The resampler is a 24-tap windowed sinc, not Apple's converter.
- **EQ:** `.lowPass` is a bilinear Butterworth. A frequency change glides log-linearly over 1440 frames.
- **Limiter:** I reverse-engineered AUPeakLimiter. Its output matches Apple's to within about 1e-5 on steps, spikes, sines and noise.
- **Player restart:** offline on macOS, a looping player behind a slowed-down varispeed stays silent after pause/start until its own timeline catches up with the engine. This is why the macOS WAVs have gaps of up to 1.25 s in the BB-8 and WALL-E runs. The facade reproduces it offline only; a real-time engine restarts its clock, so live play resumes at once on both platforms.

Live play goes through a render thread feeding a 48 kHz Godot AudioStreamGenerator, about 32 ms queued (100 ms on the headless Dummy driver). With CoreAudio, a captured test tone matched the expected level to 0.01% with no gaps.

- `--audio-smoke-test` passes all 61 checks (exit 0). It writes the s

Both modes pass (--menu-smoke-test, --hud-smoke-test), and the facade self-test output is byte-identical to before.

**New reference tool.** tools/scenekit-reference/ui-reference/build.sh compiles the macOS game's own HUD files (RaceHUD, RaceNavigationMap, SimulatorView/HUDView, FrameRateHUD) with a copy of SimulationCore. It renders the same synthetic states as --hud-smoke-test through AppKit. Its dirt-hud.png is byte-identical to the game's own smoke capture, so it is a trustworthy reference. It also gives clean HUD-only references for race-start, race-pause, race-results, the maps, the sandbox HUD and the FPS readout, which the game only captures over a 3D scene or not at all.

**What I found and fixed (measured against CoreText with a new TextCalibration.swift paired with a --text-calibration mode):**
- **Font smoothing:** CoreText thickens glyphs according to point size, the text colour's brightness (white up to 2.4 times more than black, capped at 0.71 px), and whether a control cell draws the text over a transparent background (adds 0.31 px). The background colour makes no difference. The old single setting left the selected menu button ("Sandbox", white) 13 % too light and the loading screen's labels 5–13 % too light. Ink now matches within 1.5 % on average.
- **Horizontal placement:** CoreText snaps glyphs to a size-dependent sub-pixel grid (1/5 pixel up to whole pixels). Godot's rounding to quarter pixels had put large text up to 0.6 px to the right.
- **Vertical placement:** a fractional text origin moves d

content.text:
Nine of the eleven stages in the parallel port are done. Only the town stream is still running: it's porting the crowds and residents now, then it compares its captures against the Mac ones. Everything so far sits in five separate worktrees; nothing is merged or pushed yet.

| Stream | Status | Result so far |
|---|---|---|
| **Game logic** (earlier stage) | Done, committed | Output identical to Swift, every number |
| **Robots + sandbox** | Ported, compared | Robot close-ups differ from SceneKit by under 0.4/255 with shadows off. All three robot/sandbox test modes pass. |
| **Race world + effects** | Ported, compared | Track, sky, suns, fog, walls, trails, ruts, gate and aprons within 1–6/255 of the Mac captures. With the same starting grid, the race leaves exactly the same tread marks as the Mac run. |
| **Town** | Ported; crowds/residents in progress | The generated town is **identical** to the Mac one: 497 buildings, 492 reachable compounds, 4,976 collision bodies, same triangle counts. |
| **Audio** | Ported | All 61 of the Mac game's audio checks pass. Apple's peak limiter was reverse-engineered to within about 1e-5. |
| **Interface** | Ported, compared | Menu and HUD test modes pass. A reference build of the Mac HUD code reproduces the game's own HUD capture byte for byte, so the comparison is trustworthy. |

**Known gaps:**
- **Waiting on other parts:** several comparisons can't finish until the parts are merged. Examples: the menu needs the real robots; the sandstorm checks and race lap times need the real town's collision world.
- **Shadows:** SceneKit's shadow speckle on some walls isn't reproduced, and shadow edges sit about 5 cm off.
- **Ambient occlusion:** still about 9% different on low walls.
- **Performance:**
  - The deformable sand costs about 12.5 ms per frame in Godot, against 7.3 ms on the Mac.
  - The town build takes about 13 s in the unoptimised debug build, against 4 s in the Mac's optimised Swift. I haven't timed an optimised Godot build yet.

**Next:** once the town stream finishes, I'll merge all five worktrees, remove the temporary stubs, and port the main game loop (`App.swift`: session, race control, camera, input, settings, scores). Then I'll compare the full game against the Mac version.

Sorry, that was sloppy wording: nothing went to `main`. By "main branch" I meant the branch we've been working on, `codex/mos-aster-racing-city`. `origin/main` is unchanged: its latest commit is still a teammate's from 2026-10-01, and none of the Godot work is in it.

**Pushed:**
- `codex/mos-aster-racing-city` at `3dbde0d`: the Godot skeleton, the C# core with its checks, the SceneKit compatibility layer and the test-mode registry. Before pushing I rebased onto two new commits a teammate had pushed there, which touch Mac diagnostics only.
- Five new branches holding each stream's committed work: `godot-port/robots`, `godot-port/race-world`, `godot-port/town`, `godot-port/audio` and `godot-port/ui`.
- `godot-port/town-uncommitted`: a snapshot of the town agent's unsaved work, because that agent is still running.

**Blocked:** the background job that would re-push all of that every 10 minutes. The permission check refused it as a destructive git action, because the job force-updates the backup branches each time. I haven't worked around it. Two ways forward:
- Allow it by adding a Bash permission rule for force-pushes to `godot-port/*`, and I'll start the 10-minute job.
- Or I push each stream's branch whenever one of its agents commits. That way, a crash mid-stage would lose that stage's uncommitted work.

**Provenance caveat:** the `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer on `3dbde0d` reuses this session's earlier checkpoint. Entire didn't capture anything new for it, because this repo only has Entire hooks for Codex, not Claude Code. Running `entire agent add claude-code` yourself would fix that for future commits.

Which backup option do you want?

content.thinking: I'm adding a post-commit hook, chained after the Git LFS one, that backs up each agent worktree branch to its `godot-port/<stream>` branch via a non-forced background push, keeping commits fast.

input.command:
cd /Users/m1/marvin/.git && python3 - <<'EOF'
open('hooks/post-commit.backup-push','w').write(r'''#!/bin/sh
# After a commit on an agent worktree branch (worktree-*), push it to origin as godot-port/<stream>
# so a machine crash cannot lose committed work. Plain (non-force) push, in the background.
branch=$(git symbolic-ref --short -q HEAD) || exit 0
case "$branch" in worktree-*) ;; *) exit 0 ;; esac
common=$(git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir)
name=$(awk -v b="$branch" '$1==b {print $2}' "$common/godot-port-names" 2>/dev/null)
[ -n "$name" ] || name=${branch#worktree-}
head=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
(
  PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:/opt/homebrew/bin:$PATH" GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 \
  git -c credential.helper= -c "credential.helper=!$HOME/.local/bin/gh auth git-credential" \
    push --porcelain origin "$head:refs/heads/godot-port/$name" 2>&1 | grep -E '^[!*= +-]|error' |
    sed "s|^|$(date '+%F %T') $name |" >> "$common/backup-push.log"
) >/dev/null 2>&1 &
exit 0
''')
open('godot-port-names','w').write('''worktree-wf_d2ac9938-817-1 robots
worktree-wf_d2ac9938-817-2 race-world
worktree-wf_d2ac9938-817-3 town
worktree-wf_d2ac9938-817-4 audio
worktree-wf_d2ac9938-817-5 ui
''')
p='hooks/post-commit.pre-entire'; s=open(p).read()
if 'post-commit.backup-push' not in s:
    s=s.replace('git lfs post-commit "$@"\n','git lfs post-commit "$@"\n"$(dirname "$0")/post-commit.backup-push" || true\n')
    open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF
chmod +x hooks/post-commit.backup-push && command cat hooks/post-commit.pre-entire

name: push-on-commit-marvin
description: In the entireio/marvin repo, push every branch as soon as it commits, and attach Entire checkpoints manually when hooks aren't capturing
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

Push every branch whenever it commits; don't batch pushes until a milestone. Agent worktree branches (`worktree-*`) go to `godot-port/<stream>` on origin. A local post-commit hook does this automatically: `.git/hooks/post-commit.backup-push` with the name map in `.git/godot-port-names`. Force pushes and periodic force-push loops were refused by the permission classifier, so use plain pushes only.

Call branches by their name (e.g. `codex/mos-aster-racing-city`), never "main", unless the branch really is `main`.

**Why:** the user wants no work lost if the machine crashes. They were alarmed when "main branch" was used loosely, because pushes go to the working branch, not `main`.

**How to apply:** after each commit on `codex/mos-aster-racing-city`, run `entire session attach <session-id> --force` (from `~/.local/bin/entire`) while this session's hooks aren't capturing, then push and verify that the branch and checkpoint refs are on origin. Related: [[no-effort-estimates]].

content.text:
No, I haven't broken the Entire config. Here's what's in the repo and what's only on this Mac.

**Committed, so it applies on every machine:**
- **`.claude/settings.json`:** exactly what `entire enable --agent claude-code` generates, unedited. Its hooks call `entire` by name, the same as the Codex hooks already in the repo, so they work wherever `entire` is installed and on `PATH`.
- **`.entire/settings.json`:** unchanged. Entire also wrote a setting that bakes this Mac's binary path into git hooks. I reverted it precisely because it would have been wrong on other machines.
- **`.gitignore`:** now ignores `.claude/worktrees/`.

**Only on this Mac, not in git:**
- **Git hooks in `.git/hooks`:** Entire's standard hooks plus the existing Git LFS ones. Any machine gets these from `entire enable`.
- **The backup-push hook:** pushes each port worktree to `godot-port/<stream>` on commit.
- **Two links in `~/.local/bin`, to `entire` and `git-lfs`:** these are the `PATH` workaround.

**The `PATH` issue is specific to this Mac:**
- This Claude Code process was started without `/opt/homebrew/bin` on its `PATH`. Your `~/.zshrc` adds Homebrew only in interactive shells, and `/etc/paths.d/homebrew` only applies to login shells.
- My shells and any git hooks they trigger inherit the process's `PATH`. So without the links, Entire's hooks would silently skip and LFS would warn on every commit.
- The links are a local, reversible workaround. The cleaner fix is starting Claude Code from a terminal where Homebrew is already on `PATH`.

**Pushed and verified on origin:** `codex/mos-aster-racing-city` at `03d6d19`, plus the five `godot-port/*` stream branches. The hook now pushes each stream branch whenever one of its agents commits.

**Entire capture is still incomplete.** Entire marked this session "ended" after its first 10 turns (2026-10-03). A manual attach can only re-link that old checkpoint, so nothing after the clone is captured, including the Godot port. New Claude Code sessions started inside `/Users/m1/marvin` will be captured automatically by the hooks now installed. For this session there's no legitimate way to fix it short of changing Entire's internal session state, which I haven't done.

The town stream is still porting crowds and residents; after that comes the merge and the main game loop.

content.text:
It's by design in the Entire CLI version installed here (0.11.3), not a misconfiguration. I read its source to confirm.

- **`attach` is a one-time import.** In `cmd/entire/cli/attach.go:242-258`, if the session's local Entire state already records a checkpoint, `attach` prints "already has checkpoint" and adds that same checkpoint ID to the new commit. It never re-reads the transcript.
- **This session got its checkpoint on 2026-10-03.** That was my first attach, after the brick-wall fix, when the session had 10 turns. Entire marked it "ended" at that point, so every later attach re-links that snapshot. `entire session info` confirms it: 10 turns, last active 2026-10-03.
- **Why the hooks never tracked it:** this session started in `/Users/m1`, which isn't a git repo, and only later moved into `marvin`. Entire has an open issue for this case: entireio/cli#1439, "Agent sessions should adopt enabled repos when a long session switches git common dirs".

What that means in practice:
- New Claude Code sessions started inside `/Users/m1/marvin` will be captured automatically by the hooks now installed.
- For this session, Entire has no supported way to update the attached checkpoint. The only workaround is editing Entire's local session state so `attach` treats it as new. That's internal state I'd rather not modify without your go-ahead, and I haven't verified it would work cleanly, because the commits already carry the old checkpoint ID.

Do you want me to try that workaround, or file an issue on entireio/cli asking for an attach that refreshes an existing checkpoint?
